title: Early heretics from Simon Magus onward; Philoponus; V. nearly all prior-century heretics denied flesh-resurrection
pass_a_gloss: In sum, if we unroll ecclesiastical history and the authors who wrote on heresies by design, it stands as plain that nearly all the heretics belonging toward the prior ages denied the resurrection belonging toward the flesh. V. Johannes Philoponus the Grammarian wrote a book On the Resurrection in which he takes away the resurrection of bodies and speaks many things inconsiderately, even mocking the holy fathers, as Photius notes. Add to him Theodoret (Heretical Fables book 1). touching each see Epiphanius bishop of Cyprus, who teaches that from Simon Magus, parent and leader belonging toward the heretics in the New Testament Church, the resurrection stood as denied, and that the sects born from him persisted in this error. Toward the end of On Prescriptions he indicates that in the first ages heretics attacked this article belonging toward our faith — namely Saturninus, Basilides, the Ophites, Carpocrates, Cerinthus, Valentinus, Ptolemy, Secundus, Marcus, and Colarbasus, Cerdo and his disciple Marcion of Pontus, Lucian, Apelles.
pass_b_english: Toward the end of On Prescriptions he indicates that in the first ages heretics attacked this article of our faith — namely Saturninus, Basilides, the Ophites, Carpocrates, Cerinthus, Valentinus, Ptolemy, Secundus, Marcus, and Colarbasus, Cerdo and his disciple Marcion of Pontus, Lucian, Apelles. Concerning each see Epiphanius bishop of Cyprus, who teaches that from Simon Magus, parent and leader of the heretics in the New Testament Church, the resurrection was denied, and that the sects born from him persisted in this error. Add to him Theodoret (Heretical Fables book 1). Johannes Philoponus the Grammarian wrote a book On the Resurrection in which he takes away the resurrection of bodies and speaks many things inconsiderately, even mocking the holy fathers, as Photius notes.
V. In sum, if we unroll ecclesiastical history and the authors who wrote on heresies by design, it is plain that nearly all the heretics of the prior ages denied the resurrection of the flesh.
source_text: Sub finem libri de praescriptionibus indicat, primis saeculis haereticos hunc fidei nostrae articulum impugnasse, Saturninum videlicet, Basilidem, Ophitas, Carpocratem, Cerinthum, Valentinum, Ptolomaeum, Secundum, Marcum, & Colarbasum, Cerdonem ejusque discipulum Marcionem Ponticum, Lucianum, Apellem. De singulis videas Epiphanium episcopum Cyprium, qui a Simone Mago haereticorum in N.T. Ecclesia parente & duce, resurrectionem negatam docet, sectasque ab ipso natas in hoc errore perstitisse. Cui adde Theodoretum lib. 1. haereticarum fabularum. Johannes Philoponus Grammaticus librum de resurrectione scripsit, in quo corporum resurrectionem tollit, & multa inconsiderate loquitur, sanctos etiam patres irridens, ut notat Photius. V. In summa, si historiam Ecclesiasticam evolvamus, & authores, qui de haeresibus ex instituto scripserunt, palam sit, priorum saeculorum haereticos ferme omnes carnis resurrectionem negavisse.
